mixer: One who, or that which, mixes.
minimus: 1. A being of the smallest size. (old) Shak. 2. (Anat.) The little finger; the fifth digit, or that corresponding to it, in either the manus or pes.
millefioreglass: Slender rods or tubes of colored glass fused together and embedded in clear glass; -- used for paperweights and other small articles.
minimum: The least quantity assignable, admissible, or possible, in a given case; hence, a thing of small consequence; -- opposed to Ant: maximum.
misbecome: Not to become; to suit ill; not to befit or be adapted to. Macaulay. Thy father will not act what misbecomes him. Addison.
misapply: To apply wrongly; to use for a wrong purpose; as, to misapply a name or title; to misapply public money.
mirza: The common title of honor in Persia, prefixed to the surname of an individual. When appended to the surname, it signifies Prince.
midday: The middle part of the day; noon. | Of or pertaining to noon; meridional; as, the midday sun.
mis: A prefix used adjectively and adverbially in the sense of amiss, wrong, ill, wrongly, unsuitably; as, misdeed, mislead, mischief, miscreant.
micro: A combining form signifying: (a) Small, little, trivial, slight; as, microcosm, microscope. (b) (Metric System, Elec., Mech., etc.) A millionth part of; as, microfarad, microohm, micrometer.
misfaith: Want of faith; distrust. "[Anger] born of your misfaith." Tennyson.
microform: A microscopic form of life; an animal or vegetable organism microscopic size.
mistrust: Want of confidence or trust; suspicion; distrust. Milton. | 1. To regard with jealousy or suspicion; to suspect; to doubt the integrity of; to distrust. I will never mistrust my wife again. Shak. 2. To forebode as near, or likely to occur; to surmise.
mirage: An optical effect, sometimes seen on the ocean, but more frequently in deserts, due to total reflection of light at the surface common to two strata of air differently heated. The reflected image is seen, commonly in an inverted position, while the real object may or may not be in sight.
michaelmas: The feat of the archangel Michael, a church festival, celebrated on the 29th of September. Hence, colloquially, autumn. Michaelmas daisy. (Bot.) See under Daisy.
midway: The middle of the way or distance; a middle way or course. Shak. Paths indirect, or in the midway faint. Milton. | Being in the middle of the way or distance; as, the midway air. Shak.
misrecollect: To have an erroneous remembrance of; to suppose erroneously that one recollects. Hitchcock.
misemploy: To employ amiss; as, to misemploy time, advantages, talents, etc. Their frugal father's gains they misemploy. Dryden.
misgive: 1. To give or grant amiss. (old) Laud. 2. Specifically: To give doubt and apprehension to, instead of confidence and courage; to impart fear to; to make irresolute; | To give out doubt and apprehension; to be fearful or irresolute. "My mind misgives." Shak.
microscope: An optical instrument, consisting of a lens, or combination of lenses, for making an enlarged image of an object which is too minute to be viewed by the naked eye.
mira: A remarkable variable star in the constellation Cetus (o Ceti).
milkvetch: A leguminous herb (Astragalus glycyphyllos) of Europe and Asia, supposed to increase the secretion of milk in goats. Note: The name is sometimes taken for the whole genus Astragalus, of which there are about two hundred species in North America, and even more elsewhere.
misgovernment: Bad government; want of government. Shak.
mistaker: One who mistakes. Well meaning ignorance of some mistakers. Bp. Hall.
misapprehension: A mistaking or mistake; wrong apprehension of one's meaning of a fact; misconception; misunderstanding.
mistura: (a) A mingled compound in which different ingredients are contained in a liquid state; a mixture. See Mixture, n., 4. (b) Sometimes, a liquid medicine containing very active substances, and which can only be administered by drops. Dunglison.
microtomy: The art of using the microtome; investigation carried on with the microtome.
minutely: In a minute manner; with minuteness; exactly; nicely. | Happening every minute; continuing; unceasing. (old) Throwing themselves absolutely upon God's minutely providence. Hammond.
misgiving: Evil premonition; doubt; distrust. "Suspicious and misgivings." South.
mint: The name of several aromatic labiate plants, mostly of the genus Mentha, yielding odoriferous essential oils by distillation. See Mentha. Note: Corn mint is Mentha arvensis. -- Horsemint is M. | 1. A place where money is coined by public authority. 2. Hence: Any place regarded as a source of unlimited supply; the supply itself. A mint of phrases in his brain. Shak.
miseducate: To educate in a wrong manner.
misconfident: Having a mistaken confidence; wrongly trusting. Bp. Hall.
misrepute: To have in wrong estimation; to repute or estimate erroneously.
misprint: A mistake in printing; a deviation from the copy; as, a book full of misprints.
miscredent: A miscreant, or believer in a false religious doctrine. (old) Holinshed.
microphthalmia: An unnatural smallness of the eyes, occurring as the result of disease or of imperfect development.
mistletoe: A parasitic evergreen plant of Europe (Viscum album), bearing a glutinous fruit. When found upon the oak, where it is rare, it was an object of superstitious regard among the Druids. A bird lime is prepared from its fruit. [Written also misletoe, misseltoe, and mistleto.] Lindley. Loudon.
mimosa: A genus of leguminous plants, containing many species, and including the sensitive plants (Mimosa sensitiva, and M. pudica). Note: The term mimosa is also applied in commerce to several kinds bark imported from Australia, and used in tanning; -- called also wattle bark. Tomlinson.
microscopist: One skilled in, or given to, microscopy.
mismanagement: Wrong or bad management; as, he failed through mismagement.
milldam: A dam or mound to obstruct a water course, and raise the water to a height sufficient to turn a mill wheel.
micraster: A genus of sea urchins, similar to Spatangus, abounding in the chalk formation; -- from the starlike disposal of the ambulacral furrows.
misdistinguish: To make wrong distinctions in or concerning. Hooker.
miscredulity: Wrong credulity or belief; misbelief. Bp. Hall.
miny: Abounding with mines; like a mine. "Miny caverns." Thomson.
milord: Lit., my lord; hence (as used on the Continent), an English nobleman or gentleman.
milligram: A measure of weight, in the metric system, being the thousandth part of a gram, equal to the weight of a cubic millimeter of water, or .01543 of a grain avoirdupois.
misrepeat: To repeat wrongly; to give a wrong version of. Gov. Winthrop.
mister: A title of courtesy prefixed to the name of a man or youth. It is usually written in the abbreviated form Mr. To call your name, inquire your where, Or whet you think of Mister Some-one's book, Or… | To address or mention by the title Mr.; as, he mistered me in a formal way. [Colloq.]
midweek: The middle of the week. Also used adjectively.
mischiefmaker: One who makes mischief; one who excites or instigates quarrels or enmity.
mise: 1. (Law) The issue in a writ of right. 2. Expense; cost; disbursement. (old) 3. A tax or tallage; in Wales, an honorary gift of the people to a new king or prince of Wales; also, a tribute paid, in the country palatine of Chester, England, at the change of the owner of the earldom. (old)
misstep: A wrong step; an error of conduct. | To take a wrong step; to go astray.
miscreancy: The quality of being miscreant; adherence to a false religion; false faith. (old) Ayliffe.
miner: 1. One who mines; a digger for metals, etc.; one engaged in the business of getting ore, coal, or precious stones, out of the earth; one who digs military mines; as, armies have sappers and miners. 2. (Zoöl.) (a) Any of numerous insects which, in the larval state, excavate galleries in the parenchyma of leaves. They are mostly minute moths and dipterous flies.
miserableness: The state or quality of being miserable.
microbacteria: In the classification of Cohn, one of the four tribes of Bacteria. Note: In this classification bacteria are divided into four tribes: 1. Spherobacteria, or spherical bacteria, as the genus Micrococcus. 2. Microbacteria, or bacteria in the form of short rods, including the genus Bacterium. 3.
misy: An impure yellow sulphate of iron; yellow copperas or copiapite.
ministry: 1. The act of ministering; ministration; service. "With tender ministry." Thomson. 2. Hence: Agency; instrumentality. The ordinary ministry of second causes. Atterbury. The wicked ministry of arms. Dryden. 3. The office, duties, or functions of a minister, servant, or agent; ecclesiastical, executive, or ambassadorial function or profession. 4. The body of ministers of state;
miscreated: Formed unnaturally or illegitimately; deformed. Spenser. Milton.
mite: 1. (Zoöl.) A minute arachnid, of the order Acarina, of which there are many species; as, the cheese mite, sugar mite, harvest mite, etc. See Acarina. 2. Etym: [D. mijt; prob. the same word.] A small coin formerly circulated in England, rated at about a third of a farthing. The name is also applied to a small coin used in Palestine in the time of Christ.
millier: A weight of the metric system, being one million grams; a metric ton.
misbehavior: Improper, rude, or uncivil behavior; ill conduct. Addison.
mission: 1. The act of sending, or the state of being sent; a being sent or delegated by authority, with certain powers for transacting business; comission. Whose glorious deeds, but in these fields of late,… | To send on a mission. [Mostly used in the form of the past participle.] Keats.
ministrant: Performing service as a minister; attendant on service; acting under command; subordinate. "Princedoms and dominations ministrant." Milton. -- n. One who ministers.
mickle: Much; great. [Written also muckle and mockle.] [Old Eng. & Scot.] "A man of mickle might." Spenser.
mislay: 1. To lay in a wrong place; to ascribe to a wrong source. The fault is generally mislaid upon nature. Locke. 2. To lay in a place not recollected; to lose. The... charter, indeed, was unfortunately mislaid: and the prayer of their petition was to obtain one of like import in its stead. Hallam.
mineralizer: An element which is combined with a metal, thus forming an ore. Thus, in galena, or lead ore, sulphur is a mineralizer; in hematite, oxygen is a mineralizer.
miliolitic: Of or pertaining to the genus Miliola; containing miliolites.
mistressship: 1. Female rule or dominion. 2. Ladyship, a style of address; -- with the personal pronoun. (old) Massinger.
millennialism: Belief in, or expectation of, the millennium; millenarianism.
missingly: With a sense of loss. (old) Shak.
misreport: To report erroneously; to give an incorrect account of. Locke. | An erroneous report; a false or incorrect account given. Denham. South.
misinterpretable: Capable of being misinterpreted; liable to be misunderstood.
mill: A money of account of the United States, having the value of the tenth of a cent, or the thousandth of a dollar. | 1. A machine for grinding or commuting any substance, as grain, by rubbing and crushing it between two hard, rough, or intented surfaces; as, a gristmill, a coffee mill; a bone mill. 2.
micrological: Of or pertaining to micrology; very minute; as, micrologic examination. -- Mi`cro*log"ic*al*ly, adv.
microtomical: Of or pert. to the microtome or microtomy; cutting thin slices.
mich: To lie hid; to skulk; to act, or carry one's self, sneakingly. [Obs. or Colloq.] [Written also meach and meech.] Spenser.
misbeliever: One who believes wrongly; one who holds a false religion. Shak.
miscolor: To give a wrong color to; figuratively, to set forth erroneously or unfairly; as, to miscolor facts. C. Kingsley.
missish: Like a miss; prim; affected; sentimental. -- Miss"ish*ness, n.
minikin: 1. A little darling; a favorite; a minion. (old) Florio. 2. A little pin. (old)
mizzle: 1. To rain in very fine drops. Spenser. 2. To take one's self off; to go. [Slang] As long as George the Fourth could reign, he reigned, And then he mizzled. Epigram, quoted by Wright.
middlemost: Being in the middle, or nearest the middle; midmost.
mittened: Covered with a mitten or mittens. "Mittened hands." Whittier.
microlestes: An extinct genus of small Triassic mammals, the oldest yet found in European strata.
millionairess: A woman who is a millionaire, or the wife of a millionaire. [Humorous] Holmes.
mile: A certain measure of distance, being equivalent in England and the United States to 320 poles or rods, or 5,280 feet. Note: The distance called a mile varies greatly in different countries. Its length in yards is, in Norway, 12,182; in Brunswick, 11,816; in Sweden, 11,660; in Hungary, 9,139; in Switzerland, 8,548; in Austria, 8,297; in Prussia, 8,238; in Poland, 8,100;
misfortune: Bad fortune or luck; calamity; an evil accident; disaster; mishap; mischance. Consider why the change was wrought, You 'll find his misfortune, not his fault. Addison. Syn. -- Calamity; mishap; | To happen unluckily or unfortunately; to miscarry; to fail. (old) Stow.
misalliance: A marriage with a person of inferior rank or social station; an improper alliance; a mesalliance. A Leigh had made a misalliance, and blushed A Howard should know it. Mrs. Browning.
millrind: A figure supposed to represent the iron which holds a millstone by being set into its center.
ministration: The act of ministering; service; ministry. "The days of his ministration." Luke i. 23.
minister: 1. A servant; a subordinate; an officer or assistant of inferior rank; hence, an agent, an instrument. Moses rose up, and his minister Joshua. Ex. xxiv. 13. I chose Camillo for the minister, to… | To furnish or apply; to afford; to supply; to administer. He that ministereth seed to the sower. 2 Cor. ix. 10. We minister to God reason to suspect us. Jer. Taylor.
miasma: Infectious particles or germs floating in the air; air made noxious by the presence of such particles or germs; noxious effluvia; malaria.
mistradition: A wrong tradition. "Monsters of mistradition." Tennyson.
mischiefmaking: Causing harm; exciting enmity or quarrels. Rowe. -- n. The act or practice of making mischief, inciting quarrels, etc.
microbiology: The study of minute organisms, or microbes, as the bacteria. -- Mi`cro*bi`o*log"ic*al (#), a. -- Mi`cro*bi*ol"o*gist (#), n.
mitten: 1. A covering for the hand, worn to defend it from cold or injury. It differs from a glove in not having a separate sheath for each finger. Chaucer. 2. A cover for the wrist and forearm. To give the mitten to, to dismiss as a lover; to reject the suit of. [Colloq.] -- To handle without mittens, to treat roughly; to handle without gloves. [Colloq.]
misnomer: The misnaming of a person in a legal instrument, as in a complaint or indictment; any misnaming of a person or thing; a wrong or inapplicable name or title. Many of the changes, by a great misnomer, called parliamentary "reforms". Burke. The word "synonym" is fact a misnomer. Whatel
miniate: To paint or tinge with red lead or vermilion; also, to decorate with letters, or the like, painted red, as the page of a manuscript. T. Wharton. | Of or pertaining to the color of red lead or vermilion; painted with vermilion.
mistake: 1. To take or choose wrongly. [Obs. or R.] Shak. 2. To take in a wrong sense; to misunderstand misapprehend, or misconceive; as, to mistake a remark; to mistake one's meaning. Locke. | To err in knowledge, perception, opinion, or judgment; to commit an unintentional error. Servants mistake, and sometimes occasion misunderstanding among friends. Swift.
misween: To ween amiss; to misjudge; to distrust; to be mistaken. (old) Spenser.
miscall: 1. To call by a wrong name; to name improperly. 2. To call by a bad name; to abuse. (old) Fuller.
misthink: To think wrongly. (old) "Adam misthought of her." Milton. | To have erroneous thoughts or judgment of; to think ill of. (old) Shak.
minor: 1. Inferior in bulk, degree, importance, etc.; less; smaller; of little account; as, minor divisions of a body. 2. (Mus.) Less by a semitone in interval or difference of pitch; as, a minor third. | 1. A person of either sex who has not attained the age at which full civil rights are accorded; an infant; in England and the United States, one under twenty-one years of age.
militia: 1. In the widest sense, the whole military force of a nation, including both those engaged in military service as a business, and those competent and available for such service; specifically, the body of citizens enrolled for military instruction and discipline, but not subject to be called into actual service except in emergencies.
misprofess: To make a false profession; to make pretensions to skill which is not possessed. | To make a false profession of.
midrash: A talmudic exposition of the Hebrew law, or of some part of it.
mixen: A compost heap; a dunghill. Chaucer. Tennyson.
mistrustful: Having or causing mistrust, suspicions, or forebodings. Their light blown out in some mistrustful wood. Shak. -- Mis*trust"ful*ly, adv. -- Mis*trust"ful*ness, n.
micrometry: The art of measuring with a micrometer.
minimization: The act or process of minimizing. Bentham.
microbicide: Any agent detrimental to, or destructive of, the life of microbes or bacterial organisms.
miocene: Of or pertaining to the middle division of the Tertiary. -- n. The Miocene period. See Chart of Geology.
mistrial: A false or erroneous trial; a trial which has no result.
mistransport: To carry away or mislead wrongfully, as by passion. (old) Bp. Hall.
mintman: One skilled in coining, or in coins; a coiner.
missa: The service or sacrifice of the Mass.
missay: 1. To say wrongly. 2. To speak evil of; to slander. (old)
micronometer: An instrument for noting minute portions of time.
miterwort: Any plant of the genus Mitella, -- slender, perennial herbs with a pod slightly resembling a bishop's miter; bishop's cap. False miterwort, a white-flowered perennial herb of the United States (Tiarella cardifolia).
mimetic: 1. Apt to imitate; given to mimicry; imitative. 2. (Biol.) Characterized by mimicry; -- applied to animals and plants; as, mimetic species; mimetic organisms. See Mimicry.
misdo: 1. To do wrongly. Afford me place to show what recompense To wards thee I intend for what I have misdone. Milton. 2. To do wrong to; to illtreat. (old) Chaucer. | To do wrong; to commit a fault. I have misdone, and I endure the smart. Dryden.
mien: Aspect; air; manner; demeanor; carriage; bearing. Vice is a monster of so frightful mien, As, to be hated, needs but to be seen. Pope.
mitotic: Of or pertaining to mitosis; karyokinetic; as, mitotic cell division; -- opposed to amitotic. --Mi*tot"ic*al*ly (#), adv.
micropegmatite: A rock showing under the microscope the structure of a graphic granite (pegmatite). -- Mi`cro*peg`ma*tit"ic, a.
micronesian: Of or pertaining to Micronesia, a collective designation of the islands in the western part of the Pacific Ocean, embracing the Marshall and Gilbert groups, the Ladrones, the Carolines, etc.
misobserve: To observe inaccurately; to mistake in observing. Locke.
misjoinder: An incorrect union of parties or of causes of action in a procedure, criminal or civil. Wharton.
misuse: 1. To treat or use improperly; to use to a bad purpose; to misapply; as, to misuse one's talents. South. The sweet poison of misused wine. Milton. 2. To abuse; to treat ill. | 1. Wrong use; misapplication; erroneous or improper use. Words little suspected for any such misuse. Locke. 2. Violence, or its effects. (old) Shak.
misdepart: To distribute wrongly. (old) He misdeparteth riches temporal. Chaucer.
miniver: A fur esteemed in the Middle Ages as a part of costume. It is uncertain whether it was the fur of one animal only or of different animals.
misnurture: To nurture or train wrongly; as, to misnurture children. Bp. Hall.
mixtilinear: Containing, or consisting of, lines of different kinds, as straight, curved, and the like; as, a mixtilinear angle, that is, an angle contained by a straight line and a curve.
microcline: A mineral of the feldspar group, like orthoclase or common feldspar in composition, but triclinic in form.
millepore: Any coral of the genus Millepora, having the surface nearly smooth, and perforated with very minute unequal pores, or cells. The animals are hydroids, not Anthozoa. See Hydrocorallia.
misname: To call by the wrong name; to give a wrong or inappropriate name to.
minyan: A quorum, or number necessary, for conducting public worship.
milliliter: A measure of capacity in the metric system, containing the thousandth part of a liter. It is a cubic centimeter, and is equal to .061 of an English cubic inch, or to .0338 of an American fluid ounce.
midfeather: 1. (Steam Boilers) A vertical water space in a fire box or combustion chamber. 2. (Mining) A support for the center of a tunnel.
miniardize: To render delicate or dainty. (old) Howell.
microbe: A microscopic organism; -- particularly applied to bacteria and especially to pathogenic forms; as, the microbe of fowl cholera.
milliary: Of or pertaining to a mile, or to distance by miles; denoting a mile or miles. A milliary column, from which they used to compute the distance of all the cities and places of note. Evelyn.
miller: 1. One who keeps or attends a flour mill or gristmill. 2. A milling machine. 3. (Zoöl.) (a) A moth or lepidopterous insect; -- so called because the wings appear as if covered with white dust or powder, like a miller's clothes. Called also moth miller. (b) The eagle ray. (c) The hen harrier. [Prov. Eng.] Miller's thumb.
misinterpret: To interpret erroneously; to understand or to explain in a wrong sense.
miliary: 1. Like millet seeds; as, a miliary eruption. 2. (Med.) Accompanied with an eruption like millet seeds; as, a miliary fever. 3. (Zoöl.) Small and numerous; as, the miliary tubercles of Echini. | One of the small tubercles of Echini.
mismanage: To manage ill or improperly; as, to mismanage public affairs.
mitigatory: Tending to mitigate or alleviate; mitigative.
misderive: 1. To turn or divert improperly; to misdirect. (old) Bp. Hall. 2. To derive erroneously.
misshapen: Having a bad or ugly form. "The mountains are misshapen." Bentley. -- Mis*shap"en*ly, adv. -- Mis*shap"en*ness, n.
milliard: A thousand millions; -- called also billion. See Billion.
minable: Such as can be mined; as, minable earth. Sir T. North.
minutary: Pertaining to, or consisting of, minutes. (old) Fuller.
microphthalmy: An unnatural smallness of the eyes, occurring as the result of disease or of imperfect development.
minette: The smallest of regular sizes of portrait photographs.
milanese: Of or pertaining to Milan in Italy, or to its inhabitants. -- n. sing. & pl. A native or inhabitant of Milan; people of Milan.
miser: 1. A wretched person; a person afflicted by any great misfortune. (old) Spenser. The woeful words of a miser now despairing. Sir P. Sidney. 2. A despicable person; a wretch. (old) Shak. 3. A covetous, grasping, mean person; esp., one having wealth, who lives miserably for the sake of saving and increasing his hoard.
microspectroscope: A spectroscope arranged for attachment to a microscope, for observation of the spectrum of light from minute portions of any substance.
miscopy: A mistake in copying. North Am. Rev.
mitral: Pertaining to a miter; resembling a miter; as, the mitral valve between the left auricle and left ventricle of the heart.
mistreading: Misstep; misbehavior. "To punish my mistreadings." Shak.
miscellaneous: Mixed; mingled; consisting of several things; of diverse sorts; promiscuous; heterogeneous; as, a miscellaneous collection. "A miscellaneous rabble." Milton. -- Mis`cel*la"ne*ous*ly, adv. -- Mis`cel*la"ne*ous*ness, n.
milli: A prefix denoting a thousandth part of; as, millimeter, milligram, milliampère.
millimeter: A lineal measure in the metric system, containing the thousandth part of a meter; equal to .03937 of an inch. See 3d Meter.
millimicron: The thousandish part of a micron or the millionth part of a millimeter; -- a unit of length used in measuring light waves, etc.
misprision: 1. The act of misprising; misapprehension; misconception; mistake. (old) Fuller. The misprision of this passage has aided in fostering the delusive notion. Hare. 2. Neglect; undervaluing; contempt. (old) Shak. 3. (Law) A neglect, negligence, or contempt.
mischarge: To charge erroneously, as in account. -- n. A mistake in charging.
milling: The act or employment of grinding or passing through a mill; the process of fulling; the process of making a raised or intented edge upon coin, etc.; the process of dressing surfaces of various shapes with rotary cutters. See Mill.
misimprovement: Ill use or employment; use for a bad purpose.
minus: Less; requiring to be subtracted; negative; as, a minus quantity. Minus sign (Math.), the sign [-] denoting minus, or less, prefixed to negative quantities, or quantities to be subtracted. See Negative sign, under Negative.
microcephalous: Having a small head; having the cranial cavity small; -- opposed to Ant: megacephalic.
misinterpretation: The act of interpreting erroneously; a mistaken interpretation.
misseem: 1. To make a false appearance. (old) 2. To misbecome; to be misbecoming. (old) Spenser.
milvine: Of or resembling birds of the kite kind.
mightily: 1. In a mighty manner; with might; with great earnestness; vigorously; powerfully. Whereunto I also labor, striving according to his working, which worketh in me mightily. Col. i. 29. 2. To a great degree; very much. Practical jokes amused us mightily. Hawthorne.
midget: 1. (Zoöl.) A minute bloodsucking fly. [Local, U. S.] 2. A very diminutive person.
mistigri: A variety of the game of poker in which the joker is used, and called mistigris or mistigri.
minobird: An Asiatic bird (Gracula musica), allied to the starlings. It is black, with a white spot on the wings, and a pair of flat yellow wattles on the head. It is often tamed and taught to pronounce words.
mildew: A growth of minute powdery or webby fungi, whitish or of different colors, found on various diseased or decaying substances. | To taint with mildew. He... mildews the white wheat. Shak.
misplace: To put in a wrong place; to set or place on an improper or unworthy object; as, he misplaced his confidence.
mistide: To happen or come to pass unfortunately; also, to suffer evil fortune. (old)
miss: 1. A title of courtesy prefixed to the name of a girl or a woman who has not been married. See Mistress, 5. Note: There is diversity of usage in the application of this title to two or more persons… | 1. To fail of hitting, reaching, getting, finding, seeing, hearing, etc.; as, to miss the mark one shoots at; to miss the train by being late; to miss opportunites of getting knowledge;
misthought: Erroneous thought; mistaken opinion; error. (old) Spenser.
misbehave: To behave ill; to conduct one's self improperly; -- often used with a reciprocal pronoun.
minatorily: In a minatory manner; with threats.
mistakable: Liable to be mistaken; capable of being misconceived. Sir T. Browne.
misrepresentation: Untrue representation; false or incorrect statement or account; -- usually unfavorable to the thing represented; as, a misrepresentation of a person's motives. Sydney Smith. Note: In popular use, this word often conveys the idea of intentional untruth.
milkwort: A genus of plants (Polygala) of many species. The common European P. vulgaris was supposed to have the power of producing a flow of milk in nurses. Note: The species of Campanula, or bellflower, are sometimes called milkwort, from their juice.
miscellany: A mass or mixture of various things; a medley; esp., a collection of compositions on various subjects. 'T is but a bundle or miscellany of sin; sins original, and sins actual. Hewyt. | Miscellaneous; heterogeneous. (old) Bacon.
millinet: A stiff cotton fabric used by milliners for lining bonnets.
miracle: 1. A wonder or wonderful thing. That miracle and queen of genus. Shak. 2. Specifically: An event or effect contrary to the established constitution and course of things, or a deviation from the known… | To make wonderful. (old) Shak.
misdoing: A wrong done; a fault or crime; an offense; as, it was my misdoing.
microphone: An instrument for intensifying and making audible very feeble sounds. It produces its effects by the changes of intensity in an electric current, occasioned by the variations in the contact resistance of conducting bodies, especially of imperfect conductors, under the action of acoustic vibrations.
millesimal: Thousandth; consisting of thousandth parts; as, millesimal fractions.
mistic: A kind of small sailing vessel used in the Mediterranean. It is rigged partly like a xebec, and partly like a felucca.
misology: Hatred of argument or discussion; hatred of enlightenment. G. H. Lewes.
misinform: To give untrue information to; to inform wrongly. | To give untrue information; (with against) to calumniate. Bp. Montagu.
micronesians: A dark race inhabiting the Micronesian Islands. They are supposed to be a mixed race, derived from Polynesians and Papuans.
mirth: 1. Merriment; gayety accompanied with laughter; jollity. Then will I cause to cease ... from the streets of Jerusalem, the voice of mirth. Jer. vii. 34. 2. That which causes merriment. (old) Shak. Syn. -- Merriment; joyousness; gladness; fun; frolic; glee; hilarity; festivity; jollity. See Gladness.

miasmology: That department of medical science which treats of miasma.

midgarth: The middle space or region between heaven and hell, the abode of human beings; the earth.
millimetre: A lineal measure in the metric system, containing the thousandth part of a meter; equal to .03937 of an inch. See 3d Meter.

miliola: A genus of Foraminifera, having a porcelanous shell with several longitudinal chambers.
mintage: 1. The coin, or other production, made in a mint. Stamped in clay, a heavenly mintage. Sterling. 2. The duty paid to the mint for coining.
million: 1. The number of ten hundred thousand, or a thousand thousand, -- written 1,000, 000. See the Note under Hundred 2. A very great number; an indefinitely large number. middleage: Of or pertaining to the Middle Ages; mediæval.
mitriform: Having the form of a miter, or a peaked cap; as, a mitriform calyptra. Gray.

mist: 1. Visible watery vapor suspended in the atmosphere, at or near the surface of the earth; fog. 2. Coarse, watery vapor, floating or falling in visible particles, approaching the form of rain; | To cloud; to cover with mist; to dim. Shak.
misentry: An erroneous entry or charge, as of an account.

miascite: A granitoid rock containing feldspar, biotite, elæolite, and sodalite.

miscalculate: To calculate erroneously; to judge wrongly. -- Mis*cal`cu*la"tion, n.

micmacs: A tribe of Indians inhabiting Nova Scotia and New Brunswick. [Written also Mikmaks.]

minibus: A kind of light passenger vehicle, carrying four persons.
misconclusion: An erroneous inference or conclusion. Bp. Hall.

mimographer: A writer of mimes. Sir T. Herbert.

misinformer: One who gives or incorrect information.
mizzenmast: The hindmost mast of a three-masted vessel, or of a yawl-rigged vessel.

microscopical: 1. Of or pertaining to the microscope or to microscopy; made with a microscope; as, microscopic observation. 2. Able to see extremely minute objects. Why has not man a microscopic eye Pope. 3. Very small; visible only by the aid of a microscope; as, a microscopic insect.
misconsecrate: To consecrate amiss. "Misconsecrated flags." Bp. Hall.
misrepresent: To represent incorrectly (almost always, unfacorably); to give a false erroneous representation of, either maliciously, ignirantly, or carelessly. Swift. | To make an incorrect or untrue representation. Milton.
microcephalic: Having a small head; having the cranial cavity small; -- opposed to Ant: megacephalic.
migrate: 1. To remove from one country or region to another, with a view to residence; to change one's place of residence; to remove; as, the Moors who migrated from Africa into Spain; to migrate to the West. 2. To pass periodically from one region or climate to another for feeding or breeding; -- said of certain birds, fishes, and quadrupeds.
misanthrope: A hater of mankind; a misanthropist.
mistico: A kind of small sailing vessel used in the Mediterranean. It is rigged partly like a xebec, and partly like a felucca.
mithridate: An antidote against poison, or a composition in form of an electuary, supposed to serve either as a remedy or a preservative against poison; an alexipharmic; -- so called from King Mithridates, its reputed inventor. [Love is] a drop of the true elixir; no mithridate so effectual against the infection of vice. Southey.
mineralogist: 1. One versed in mineralogy; one devoted to the study of minerals. 2. (Zoöl.) A carrier shell (Phorus).
minuteman: A militiaman who was to be ready to march at a moment's notice; -- a term used in the American Revolution.
misenter: To enter or insert wrongly, as a charge in an account.
misbegot: Unlawfully or irregularly begotten; of bad origin; pernicious. "Valor misbegot." Shak.
misdirect: To give a wrong direction to; as, to misdirect a passenger, or a letter; to misdirect one's energies. Shenstone.
mitigant: Tending to mitigate; mitigating; lentitive. Johnson.
micromere: One of the smaller cells, or blastomeres, resulting from the complete segmentation of a telolecithal ovum.
midsea: The middle part of the sea or ocean. Milton. The Mid-sea, the Mediterranean Sea. (old)
misfall: To befall, as ill luck; to happen to unluckily. (old) Chaucer.
mitu: A South American curassow of the genus Mitua.
mithras: The sun god of the Persians.
mineralogically: According to the principles of, or with reference to, mineralogy.
mincing: That minces; characterized by primness or affected nicety.
misunderstander: One who misunderstands. Sir T. More.
micrometric: Belonging to micrometry; made by the micrometer. -- Mi`cro*met"ric*al*ly, adv.
mishandle: To handle ill or wrongly; to maltreat.
midgard: The middle space or region between heaven and hell; the abode of human beings; the earth. | The middle space or region between heaven and hell, the abode of human beings; the earth.
miraculize: To cause to seem to be a miracle. Shaftesbury.
mime: 1. A kind of drama in which real persons and events were generally represented in a ridiculous manner. 2. An actor in such representations.
misknow: To have a mistaken notion of or about. (old) Bp. Hall.
misease: Want of ease; discomfort; misery. (old) Chaucer.
miraculous: 1. Of the nature of a miracle; performed by supernatural power; effected by the direct agency of almighty power, and not by natural causes. 2. Supernatural; wonderful. 3. Wonder-working. "The miraculous harp." Shak. -- Mi*rac"u*lous*ly, adv. -- Mi*rac"u*lous*ness, n.
misconstruable: Such as can be misconstrued, as language or conduct. R. North.
misground: To found erroneously. "Misgrounded conceit." Bp. Hall.
milfoil: A common composite herb (Achillea Millefolium) with white flowers and finely dissected leaves; yarrow. Water milfoil (Bot.), an aquatic herb with dissected leaves (Myriophyllum).
misconstruct: To construct wrongly; to construe or interpret erroneously.
midge: 1. Any one of many small, delicate, long-legged flies of the Chironomus, and allied genera, which do not bite. Their larvæ are usually aquatic. 2. A very small fly, abundant in many parts of the United States and Canada, noted for the irritating quality of its bite. Note: The name is also applied to various other small flies. See Wheat midge, under Wheat.
milled: Having been subjected to some process of milling. Milled cloth, cloth that has been beaten in a fulling mill. -- Milled lead, lead rolled into sheets.
migratory: 1. Removing regularly or occasionally from one region or climate to another; as, migratory birds. 2. Hence, roving; wandering; nomad; as, migratory habits; a migratory life. Migratory locust (Zoöl.) See Locust. -- Migratory thrush (Zoöl.), the American robin. See Robin.
milky: 1. Consisting of, or containing, milk. Pails high foaming with a milky flood. Pope. 2. Like, or somewhat like, milk; whitish and turbid; as, the water is milky. "Milky juice." Arbuthnot. 3. Yielding milk. "Milky mothers." Roscommon. 4. Mild; tame; spiritless. Has friendship such a faint and milky heart Shak. Milky Way. (Astron.) See Galaxy, 1.
misallegation: A erroneous statement or allegation. Bp. Hall.
misrelation: Erroneous relation or narration. Abp. Bramhall.
minutia: A minute particular; a small or minor detail; -- used chiefly in the plural.
miscellane: A mixture of two or more sorts of grain; -- now called maslin and meslin. Bacon.
milkful: Full of milk; abounding with food. "Milkful vales." Sylvester.
misbecoming: Unbecoming. Milton. -- Mis`be*com"ing*ly, adv. -- Mis`be*com"ing*ness, n. Boyle.
ministerially: In a ministerial manner; in the character or capacity of a minister.
minstrel: In the Middle Ages, one of an order of men who subsisted by the arts of poetry and music, and sang verses to the accompaniment of a harp or other instrument; in modern times, a poet; a bard; a singer and harper; a musician. Chaucer.
millinery: 1. The articles made or sold by milliners, as headdresses, hats or bonnets, laces, ribbons, and the like. 2. The business of work of a milliner.
misgoverned: Ill governed, as a people; ill directed. "Rude, misgoverned hands." Shak.
misdight: Arrayed, prepared, or furnished, unsuitably. (old) Bp. Hall.
misobserver: One who misobserves; one who fails to observe properly.
mineralogy: 1. The science which treats of minerals, and teaches how to describe, distinguish, and classify them. 2. A treatise or book on this science.
milreis: A Portuguese money of account rated in the treasury department of the United States at one dollar and eight cents; also, a Brazilian money of account rated at fifty-four cents and six mills.
minieball: A conical rifle bullet, with a cavity in its base plugged with a piece of iron, which, by the explosion of the charge, is driven farther in, expanding the sides to fit closely the grooves of the barrel.
miohippus: An extinct Miocene mammal of the Horse family, closely related to the genus Anhithecrium, and having three usable hoofs on each foot.
misdirection: 1. The act of directing wrongly, or the state of being so directed. 2. (Law) An error of a judge in charging the jury on a matter of law. Mozley & W.
mithgarthr: The middle space or region between heaven and hell, the abode of human beings; the earth.
microzoospore: A small motile spore furnished with two vibratile cilia, found in certain green algæ.
misurato: Measured; -- a direction to perform a passage in strict or measured time.
misfit: 1. The act or the state of fitting badly; as, a misfit in making a coat; a ludicrous misfit. 2. Something that fits badly, as a garment. I saw an uneasy change in Mr. Micawber, which sat tightly on him, as if his new duties were a misfit. Dickens.
mimicry: 1. The act or practice of one who mimics; ludicrous imitation for sport or ridicule. 2. (Biol.) Protective resemblance; the resemblance which certain animals and plants exhibit to other animals and plants or to the natural objects among which they live, -- a characteristic which serves as their chief means of protection against enemies; imitation; mimesis; mimetism.
microorganism: Any microscopic form of life; -- particularly applied to bacteria and similar organisms, esp. such are supposed to cause infectious diseases.
midheaven: 1. The midst or middle of heaven or the sky. 2. (Astron.) The meridian, or middle line of the heavens; the point of the ecliptic on the meridian.
midas: A genus of longeared South American monkeys, including numerous species of marmosets. See Marmoset. MIDAS'S EAR Mi"das's ear". Etym: [See Midas.] (Zoöl.) A pulmonate mollusk (Auricula, or Ellobium, aurismidæ); -- so called from resemblance to a human ear.
microseme: Having the orbital index relatively small; having the orbits broad transversely; -- opposed to Ant: megaseme.
misestimate: To estimate erroneously. J. S. Mill.
missel: Mistletoe. (old) Missel bird, Missel thrush (Zoöl.), a large European thrush (Turdus viscivorus) which feeds on the berries of the mistletoe; -- called also mistletoe thrush and missel.
millennium: A thousand years; especially, thousand years mentioned in the twentieth chapter in the twentieth chapter of Revelation, during which holiness is to be triumphant throughout the world. Some believe that, during this period, Christ will reign on earth in person with his saints.
militancy: 1. The state of being militant; warfare. 2. A military spirit or system; militarism. H. Spencer.
misfeasance: A trespass; a wrong done; the improper doing of an act which a person might lawfully do. Bouvier. Wharton.
minuet: 1. A slow graceful dance consisting of a coupee, a high step, and a balance. 2. (Mus.) A tune or air to regulate the movements of the dance so called; a movement in suites, sonatas, symphonies, etc., having the dance form, and commonly in 3-4, sometimes 3-8, measure.
miscorrect: To fail or err in attempting to correct. "Scaliger miscorrects his author." Dryden.
midnightsun: The sun shining at midnight in the arctic or antarctic summer.
milch: 1. Giving milk; -- now applied only to beasts. "Milch camels." Gen. xxxii. "Milch kine." Shak. 2. Tender; pitiful; weeping. (old) Shak.
misbelieve: To believe erroneously, or in a false religion. "That misbelieving Moor." Shak.
mikado: The popular designation of the hereditary sovereign of Japan.
microbian: Of, pertaining to, or caused by, microbes; as, the microbian theory; a microbian disease.
mitiscasting: A process, invented by P. Ostberg, for producing malleable iron castings by melting wrought iron, to which from 0.05 to 0.1 per cent of aluminium is added to lower the melting point, usually in a petroleum furnace, keeping the molten metal at the bubbling point until it becomes quiet, and then pouring the molten metal into a mold lined with a special mixture consisting…
minim: 1. Anything very minute; as, the minims of existence; -- applied to animalcula; and the like. 2. The smallest liquid measure, equal to about one drop; the sixtieth part of a fluid drachm. 3. | Minute. "Minim forms." J. R. Drake.
microphyte: A very minute plant, one of certain unicellular algæ, such as the germs of various infectious diseases are believed to be.
missound: To sound wrongly; to utter or pronounce incorrectly. E,Hall.
mi: A syllable applied to the third tone of the scale of C, i. e., to E, in European solmization, but to the third tone of any scale in the American system.
minglement: The act of mingling, or the state of being mixed.
mignon: See 3d Minion. | To flatter. [R. & Obs.] Danie
millcake: The incorporated materials for gunpowder, in the form of a dense mass or cake, ready to be subjected to the process of granulation.
miliolite: A fossil shell of, or similar to, the genus Miliola. | The same Milliolitic. Miliolite limestone (Geol.), a building stone, one of the group of the Paris basin, almost entirely made up of many-chambered microscopic shells.
microzyme: A microörganism which is supposed to act like a ferment in causing or propagating certain infectious or contagious diseases; a pathogenic bacterial organism.
millennial: Of or pertaining to the millennium, or to a thousand years; as, a millennial period; millennial happiness.
millstone: One of two circular stones used for grinding grain or other substance. No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge. Deut. xxiv. 6. Note: The cellular siliceous rock called buhrstone is usually employed for millstones; also, some kinds of lava, as that Niedermendig, or other firm rock with rough texture.
minos: A king and lawgiver of Crete, fabled to be the son of Jupiter and Europa. After death he was made a judge in the Lower Regions.
millionaire: One whose wealth is counted by millions of francs, dollars, or pounds; a very rich person; a person worth a million or more. [Written also millionnaire.]
missis: A mistress; a wife; -- so used by the illiterate. G. Eliot.
misremember: To mistake in remembering; not to remember correctly. Sir T. More.
mincemeat: Minced meat; meat chopped very fine; a mixture of boiled meat, suet, apples, etc., chopped very fine, to which spices and raisins are added; -- used in making mince pie.
mislactation: Defective flow or vitiated condition of the milk.
miasmatist: One who has made a special study of miasma.
misspeak: To err in speaking. | To utter wrongly.
mirliton: A kind of musical toy into which one sings, hums, or speaks, producing a coarse, reedy sound. Trilby singing "Ben Bolt" into a mirliton was a thing to be remembered, whether one would or no! Du Maurier.
microphonics: The science which treats of the means of increasing the intensity of low or weak sounds, or of the microphone.
micella: A theoretical aggregation of molecules constituting a structural particle of protoplasm, capable of increase or diminution without change in chemical nature.
misalter: To alter wrongly; esp., to alter for the worse. Bp. Hall.
miserable: 1. Very unhappy; wretched. What hopes delude thee, miserable man Dryden. 2. Causing unhappiness or misery. What 's more miserable than discontent Shak. 3. Worthless; mean; despicable; | A miserable person. (old) Sterne.
millrynd: A figure supposed to represent the iron which holds a millstone by being set into its center.
miserably: In a miserable; unhappily; calamitously; wretchedly; meanly. They were miserably entertained. Sir P. Sidney. The fifth was miserably stabbed to death. South.
milady: Lit., my lady; hence (as used on the Continent), an English noblewoman or gentlewoman.
misworship: Wrong or false worship; mistaken practices in religion. Bp. Hall. Such hideous jungle of misworships. Carlyle.
midrib: A continuation of the petiole, extending from the base to the apex of the lamina of a leaf.
misrehearse: To rehearse or quote incorrectly. Sir T. More.
minnesinger: A love-singer; specifically, one of a class of German poets and musicians who flourished from about the middle of the twelfth to the middle of the fourteenth century. They were chiefly of noble birth, and made love and beauty the subjects of their verses.
micaceocalcareous: Partaking of the nature of, or consisting of, mica and lime; -- applied to a mica schist containing carbonate of lime.
mire: Deep mud; wet, spongy earth. Chaucer. He his rider from the lofty steed Would have cast down and trod in dirty mire. Spenser. Mire crow (Zoöl.), the pewit, or laughing gull. [Prov. | 1. To cause or permit to stick fast in mire; to plunge or fix in mud; as, to mire a horse or wagon. 2. To soil with mud or foul matter. Smirched thus and mired with infamy. Shak.
miscegenation: A mixing of races; amalgamation, as by intermarriage of black and white.
midships: In the middle of a ship; -- properly amidships. | The timbers at the broadest part of the vessel. R. H. Dana, Jr.
minimize: To reduce to the smallest part or proportion possible; to reduce to a minimum. Bentham.
ministryship: The office of a minister. Swift.
microampere: One of the smaller measures of electrical currents; the millionth part of one ampère.
microtomic: Of or pert. to the microtome or microtomy; cutting thin slices.
microcyte: One of the elementary granules found in blood. They are much smaller than an ordinary corpuscle, and are particularly noticeable in disease, as in anæmia.
mintsauce: 1. A sauce of vinegar and sugar flavored with spearmint leaves. 2. Money. [Slang, Eng.]
miscellanea: A collection of miscellaneous matters; matters of various kinds.
miff: A petty falling out; a tiff; a quarrel; offense. Fielding.
misprise: See Misprize. (old) Shak. | To mistake. (old) Shak.
middle: 1. Equally distant from the extreme either of a number of things or of one thing; mean; medial; as, the middle house in a row; a middle rank or station in life; flowers of middle summer; | The point or part equally distant from the extremities or exterior limits, as of a line, a surface, or a solid; an intervening point or part in space, time, or order of series; the midst;
mir: A Russian village community. D. M. Wallace.
minious: Of the color of red or vermilion. (old) Sir T. Browne.
miscue: A false stroke with a billiard cue, the cue slipping from the ball struck without impelling it as desired.
mistitle: To call by a wrong title.
mixogamous: Pairing with several males; -- said of certain fishes of which several males accompany each female during spawning.
misbegotten: Unlawfully or irregularly begotten; of bad origin; pernicious. "Valor misbegot." Shak.
miryachit: A nervous disease in which the patient involuntarily imitates the words or action of another.
microtasimeter: A tasimeter, especially when arranged for measuring very small extensions. See Tasimeter.
minaret: A slender, lofty tower attached to a mosque and surrounded by one or more projecting balconies, from which the summon to prayer is cried by the muezzin.
middleaged: Being about the middle of the ordinary age of man; between 30 and 50 years old.
mislight: To deceive or lead astray with a false light. Herrick.
mismake: To make or form amiss; to spoil in making. "Limping possibilities of mismade human nature." Mrs. Browning. | To make or form amiss; to spoil in making. "Limping possibilities of mismade human nature." Mrs. Browning.
misaffection: An evil or wrong affection; the state of being ill affected. (old) Bp. Hall.
minuend: The number from which another number is to be subtracted.
misty: 1. Accompained with mist; characterized by the presence of mist; obscured by, or overspread with, mist; as, misty weather; misty mountains; a misty atmosphere. 2. Obscured as if by mist; dim; obscure; clouded; as, misty sight. The more I muse therein [theology], The mistier it seemeth. Piers Plowman.
milksickness: A peculiar malignant disease, occurring in parts of the western United States, and affecting certain kinds of farm stock (esp. cows), and persons using the meat or dairy products of infected cattle. Its chief symptoms in man are uncontrollable vomiting, obstinate constipation, pain, and muscular tremors.
mitigable: Admitting of mitigation; that may be mitigated.
might: imp. of May. Etym: [AS. meahte, mihte.] | Force or power of any kind, whether of body or mind; energy or intensity of purpose, feeling, or action; means or resources to effect an object; strength; force; power; ability; capacity.
miscognize: To fail to apprehend; to misunderstand. (old) Holland.
miswander: To wander in a wrong path; to stray; to go astray. (old) Chaucer.
milieu: Environment. The intellectual and moral milieu created by multitudes of self- centered, cultivated personalities. J. A. Symonds. It is one of the great outstanding facts of his progressive relation to the elements of his social milieu. J. M. Baldwin.
mind: 1. The intellectual or rational faculty in man; the understanding; the intellect; the power that conceives, judges, or reasons; also, the entire spiritual nature; the soul; | 1. To fix the mind or thoughts on; to regard with attention; to treat as of consequence; to consider; to heed; to mark; to note. "Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate." Rom. xii.
mismate: To mate wrongly or unsuitably; as, to mismate gloves or shoes; a mismated couple.
microbion: A microscopic organism; -- particularly applied to bacteria and especially to pathogenic forms; as, the microbe of fowl cholera.
mild: Gentle; pleasant; kind; soft; bland; clement; hence, moderate in degree or quality; -- the opposite of harsh, severe, irritating, violent, disagreeable, etc.; -- applied to persons and things; as, a mild disposition; a mild eye; a mild air; a mild medicine; a mild insanity. The rosy morn resigns her light And milder glory to the noon. Waller.
mitraille: Shot or bits of iron used sometimes in loading cannon.
microscopic: 1. Of or pertaining to the microscope or to microscopy; made with a microscope; as, microscopic observation. 2. Able to see extremely minute objects. Why has not man a microscopic eye Pope. 3. Very small; visible only by the aid of a microscope; as, a microscopic insect.
microcoustic: Pertaining, or suited, to the audition of small sounds; fitted to assist hearing. | An instrument for making faint sounds audible, as to a partially deaf person.
milliampere: The thousandth part of one ampère.
mischief: 1. Harm; damage; esp., disarrangement of order; trouble or vexation caused by human agency or by some living being, intentionally or not; often, calamity, mishap; trivial evil caused by thoughtlessness, or in sport. Chaucer. Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs. Ps. lii. 2. The practice whereof shall, I hope, secure me from many mischiefs. Fuller. 2. Cause of trouble or vexation;
mitismetal: The malleable iron produced by mitis casting; -- called also simply mitis.
militarism: 1. A military state or condition; reliance on military force in administering government; a military system. 2. The spirit and traditions of military life. H. Spencer.
mistemper: To temper ill; to disorder; as, to mistemper one's head. Warner. This inundation of mistempered humor. Shak.
middleman: 1. An agent between two parties; a broker; a go-between; any dealer between the producer and the consumer; in Ireland, one who takes land of the proprietors in large tracts, and then rents it out in small portions to the peasantry. 2. A person of intermediate rank; a commoner. 3. (Mil.) The man who occupies a central position in a file of soldiers.
midland: 1. Being in the interior country; distant from the coast or seashore; as, midland towns or inhabitants. Howell. 2. Surrounded by the land; mediterranean. And on the midland sea the French had awed. | The interior or central region of a country; -- usually in the plural. Drayton.
misstayed: Having missed stays; -- said of a ship.
minaceous: Of the color of minium or red lead; miniate.
minglemangle: To mix in a disorderly way; to make a mess of. (old) Udall.
microbic: Of or pertaining to a microbe.
minish: To diminish; to lessen. The living of poor men thereby minished. Latimer.
missive: 1. Specially sent; intended or prepared to be sent; as, a letter missive. Ayliffe. 2. Missile. "The missive weapons fly." Dryden. Letters missive, letters conveying the permission, comand, or advice… | 1. That which is sent; a writing containing a message. 2. One who is sent; a messenger. (old) Shak.
miscreance: The quality of being miscreant; adherence to a false religion; false faith. (old) Ayliffe.
milden: To make mild, or milder. Lowell.
mixtilineal: Containing, or consisting of, lines of different kinds, as straight, curved, and the like; as, a mixtilinear angle, that is, an angle contained by a straight line and a curve.
misjudge: To judge erroneously or unjustly; to err in judgment; to misconstrue.
mistaught: Wrongly taught; as, a mistaught youth. L'Estrange.
minatorially: In a minatory manner; with threats.
microphytal: Pertaining to, or of the nature of, microphytes.
misdemean: To behave ill; -- with a reflexive pronoun; as, to misdemean one's self.
misquote: To quote erroneously or incorrectly. Shak.
microbarograph: An instrument for recording minor fluctuations of atmospheric pressure, as opposed to general barometric surges.
misconstruction: Erroneous construction; wrong interpretation. Bp. Stillingfleet.
micron: A measure of length; the thousandth part of one millimeter; the millionth part of a meter.
minishment: The act of diminishing, or the state of being diminished; diminution. (old)
mislead: To lead into a wrong way or path; to lead astray; to guide into error; to cause to mistake; to deceive. Trust not servants who mislead or misinform you. Bacon. To give due light To the mislead and lonely traveler. Milton. Syn. -- To delude; deceive. See Deceive.
miscomprehend: To get a wrong idea of or about; to misunderstand.
middleearth: The world, considered as lying between heaven and hell. (old) Shak.
missile: Capable of being thrown; adapted for hurling or to be projected from the hand, or from any instrument or rngine, so as to strike an object at a distance. We bend the bow, or wing the missile dart. | A weapon thrown or projected or intended to be projcted, as a lance, an arrow, or a bullet.
microcosmical: Of or pertaining to the microcosm. Microcosmic salt (Chem.), a white crystalline substance obtained by mixing solutions of sodium phosphate and ammonium phosphate, and also called hydric-sodic- ammonic-phosphate. It is a powerful flux, and is used as a substitute for borax as a blowpipe reagent in testing for the metallic oxides.
milestone: A stone serving the same purpose as a milepost.
miscensure: To misjudge. (old) Daniel. -- n. Erroneous judgment. (old) Sylvester.
misbear: To carry improperly; to carry (one's self) wrongly; to misbehave. (old) Chaucer.
misdemeanant: One guilty of a misdemeanor. Sydney Smith.
miskindle: To kindle amiss; to inflame to a bad purpose; to excite wrongly.
microcrith: The weight of the half hydrogen molecule, or of the hydrogen atom, taken as the standard in comparing the atomic weights of the elements; thus, an atom of oxygen weighs sixteen microcriths. See Crith. J. P. Cooke.
misericordia: 1. (O. Law) An amercement. Burrill. 2. (Anc. Armor.) A thin-bladed dagger; so called, in the Middle Ages, because used to give the death wound or "mercy" stroke to a fallen adversary. 3. (Eccl.) An indulgence as to food or dress granted to a member of a religious order. Shipley.
milkmaid: A woman who milks cows or is employed in the dairy.
mishnic: Of or pertaining to the Mishna.
misunderstand: To misconceive; to mistake; to miscomprehend; to take in a wrong sense.
millennist: One who believes in the millennium. (old) Johnson.
mico: A small South American monkey (Mico melanurus), allied to the marmoset. The name was originally applied to an albino variety.
minionette: Small; delicate. (old) "His minionette face." Walpole. | A size of type between nonpareil and minion; -- used in ornamental borders, etc.
misrule: 1. The act, or the result, of misruling. 2. Disorder; confusion; tumult from insubordination. Enormous riot and misrule surveyed. Pope. Abbot, or Lord, of Misrule. See under Abbot, and Lord.
microanalysis: Analysis of the structure of materials from careful observation of photomicrographs.
microhm: The millionth part of an ohm.
miasmatic: Containing, or relating to, miasma; caused by miasma; as, miasmatic diseases.
midwife: A woman who assists other women in childbirth; a female practitioner of the obstetric art. | To perform the office of midwife.
microphonic: Of or pert. to a microphone; serving to intensify weak sounds.
minum: 1. A small kind of printing type; minion. 2. (Mus.) A minim.
mispersuasion: A false persuasion; wrong notion or opinion. Dr. H. More.
mightiness: 1. The quality of being mighty; possession of might; power; greatness; high dignity. How soon this mightiness meets misery. Shak. 2. Highness; excellency; -- with a possessive pronoun, a title of dignity; as, their high mightinesses.
minierifle: A rifle adapted to minie balls.
miry: Abounding with deep mud; full of mire; muddy; as, a miry road.
militiaman: One who belongs to the militia.
microchemistry: The application of chemical tests to minute objects or portions of matter, magnified by the use of the microscopy; -- distinguished from macro-chemistry.
microseism: A feeble earth tremor not directly perceptible, but detected only by means of specially constructed apparatus. -- Mi`cro*seis"mic (#), *seis"mic*al (#), a.
microlepidoptera: A tribe of Lepidoptera, including a vast number of minute species, as the plume moth, clothes moth, etc.
minuscule: 1. Any very small, minute object. 2. A small Roman letter which is neither capital nor uncial; a manuscript written in such letters. -- a. Of the size and style of minuscules; written in minuscules. These minuscule letters are cursive forms of the earlier uncials. I. Taylor (The Alphabet).
mileage: 1. An allowance for traveling expenses at a certain rate per mile. 2. Aggregate length or distance in miles; esp., the sum of lengths of tracks or wires of a railroad company, telegraph company, etc. [Written also milage.] Constructive mileage, a mileage allowed for journeys supposed to be made, but not actually made. Bartlett.
mindful: Bearing in mind; regardful; attentive; heedful; observant. What is man, that thou art mindful of him Ps. viii. 4. I promise you to be mindful of your admonitions. Hammond. -- Mind"ful*ly, adv. -- Mind"ful*ness, n.
misacceptation: Wrong acceptation; understanding in a wrong sense.
missy: An affectionate, or contemptuous, form of miss; a young girl; a miss. -- a. Like a miss, or girl.
misfeign: To feign with an evil design. (old) Spenser.
midgut: The middle part of the alimentary canal from the stomach, or entrance of the bile duct, to, or including, the large intestine.
millwork: 1. The shafting, gearing, and other driving machinery of mils. 2. The business of setting up or of operating mill machinery.
millilitre: A measure of capacity in the metric system, containing the thousandth part of a liter. It is a cubic centimeter, and is equal to .061 of an English cubic inch, or to .0338 of an American fluid ounce.
milligramme: A measure of weight, in the metric system, being the thousandth part of a gram, equal to the weight of a cubic millimeter of water, or .01543 of a grain avoirdupois.
mineralogize: To study mineralogy by collecting and examining minerals. Miss Edgeworth.
minnow: 1. (Zoöl.) A small European fresh-water cyprinoid fish (Phoxinus lævis, formerly Leuciscus phoxinus); sometimes applied also to the young of larger kinds; -- called also minim and minny. The name is also applied to several allied American species, of the genera Phoxinus, Notropis, or Minnilus, and Rhinichthys. 2.
midsummer: The middle of summer. Shak. Midsummer daisy (Bot.), the oxeye daisy.
miscarriage: 1. Unfortunate event or issue of an undertaking; failure to attain a desired result or reach a destination. When a counselor, to save himself, Would lay miscarriages upon his prince. Dryden. 2. Ill conduct; evil or improper behavior; as, the failings and miscarriages of the righteous. Rogers. 3. The act of bringing forth before the time; premature birth.
mirabilary: One who, or a work which, narrates wonderful things; one who writes of wonders. (old) Bacon.
miniature: 1. Originally, a painting in colors such as those in mediæval manuscripts; in modern times, any very small painting, especially a portrait. 2. Greatly diminished size or form; reduced scale. 3. | Being on a small; much reduced from the reality; as, a miniature copy.
mistigris: A variety of the game of poker in which the joker is used, and called mistigris or mistigri.
miserere: 1. (R. C. Ch.) The psalm usually appointed for penitential acts, being the 50th psalm in the Latin version. It commences with the word miserere. 2. A musical composition adapted to the 50th psalm. Where only the wind signs miserere. Lowell. 3. (Arch.) A small projecting boss or bracket, on the under side of the hinged seat of a church stall (see Stall).
miargyrite: A mineral of an iron-black color, and very sectile, consisting principally of sulphur, antimony, and silver.
minimumthermometer: , a thermometer for recording the lowest temperature since its last adjustment.
misedition: An incorrect or spurious edition. (old) Bp. Hall.
mince: 1. To cut into very small pieces; to chop fine; to hash; as, to mince meat. Bacon. 2. To suppress or weaken the force of; to extenuate; to palliate; to tell by degrees, instead of directly and… | 1. To walk with short steps; to walk in a prim, affected manner. The daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes,... mincing as they go. Is. iii. 16. I 'll...
midmain: The middle part of the main or sea. (poetic) Chapman.
minx: 1. A pert or a wanton girl. Shak. 2. A she puppy; a pet dog. (old) Udall. | The mink; -- called also minx otter. (old)
mingle: 1. To mix; intermix; to combine or join, as an individual or part, with other parts, but commonly so as to be distinguishable in the product; to confuse; to confound. There was... fire mingled with the hail. Ex. ix. 24. 2. To associate or unite in society or by ties of relationship; to cause or allow to intermarry; to intermarry.
misvalue: To value wrongly or too little; to undervalue. But for I am so young, I dread my work Wot be misvalued both of old and young. W. Browne.
microfarad: The millionth part of a farad.
mistress: 1. A woman having power, authority, or ownership; a woman who exercises authority, is chief, etc.; the female head of a family, a school, etc. The late queen's gentlewoman! a knight's daughter! To be… | To wait upon a mistress; to be courting. (old) Donne.
miscellanarian: Of or pertaining to miscellanies. Shaftesbury. -- n. A writer of miscellanies.
miscount: To count erroneously. | An erroneous counting.
middlings: 1. A combination of the coarser parts of ground wheat the finest bran, separated from the fine flour and coarse bran in bolting; -- formerly regarded as valuable only for feed; but now, after separation of the bran, used for making the best quality of flour. Middlings contain a large proportion of gluten. 2.
minded: Disposed; inclined; having a mind. Joseph... was minded to put her away privily. Matt. i. 19. If men were minded to live virtuously. Tillotson. Note: Minded is much used in composition; as, high-minded, feeble- minded, sober-minded, double-minded.
microcosmography: Description of man as a microcosm.
milkweed: Any plant of the genera Asclepias and Acerates, abounding in a milky juice, and having its seed attached to a long silky down; silkweed. The name is also applied to several other plants with a milky juice, as to several kinds of spurge.
miserly: Like a miser; very covetous; sordid; niggardly. Syn. -- Avaricious; niggardly; sordid; parsimonious; penurious; covetous; stingy; mean. See Avaricious.
minutejack: 1. A figure which strikes the hour on the bell of some fanciful clocks; -- called also jack of the clock house. 2. A timeserver; an inconstant person. Shak.
misconstrue: To construe wrongly; to interpret erroneously. Do not, great sir, misconstrue his intent. Dryden. Much afflicted to find his actions misconstrued. Addison.
minify: 1. To make small, or smaller; to diminish the apparent dimensions of; to lessen. 2. To degrade by speech or action.
mispoint: To point improperly; to punctuate wrongly.
mildness: The quality or state of being mild; as, mildness of temper; the mildness of the winter.
mirror: 1. A looking-glass or a speculum; any glass or polished substance that forms images by the reflection of rays of light. And in her hand she held a mirror bright, Wherein her face she often viewèd fair. Spenser. 2. That which gives a true representation, or in which a true image may be seen; hence, a pattern; an exemplar. She is mirour of all courtesy. Chaucer.
micturition: The act of voiding urine; also, a morbidly frequent passing of the urine, in consequence of disease.
mistral: A violent and cold northwest wind experienced in the Mediterranean provinces of France, etc.
miching: Hiding; skulking; cowardly. [Colloq.] [Written also meaching and meeching.]
ministerialist: A supporter of the ministers, or the party in power.
misshape: To shape ill; to give an ill or unnatural from to; to deform. "Figures monstrous and misshaped." Pope.
midship: Of or pertaining to, or being in, the middle of a ship. Midship beam (Naut.), the beam or timber upon which the broadest part of a vessel is formed. -- Midship bend, the broadest frame in a vessel. Weale.
misdisposition: Erroneous disposal or application. Bp. Hall.
mishna: A collection or digest of Jewish traditions and explanations of Scripture, forming the text of the Talmud. [Written also Mischna.]
misapplication: A wrong application. Sir T. Browne.
missal: The book containing the service of the Mass for the entire year; a Mass book. | Of or pertaining to the Mass, or to a missal or Mass book. Bp. Hall.
miasmatical: Containing, or relating to, miasma; caused by miasma; as, miasmatic diseases.
mining: The act or business of making mines or of working them. | Of or pertaining to mines; as, mining engineer; mining machinery; a mining region. Mining engineering. See the Note under Engineering.
mitigate: 1. To make less severe, intense, harsh, rigorous, painful, etc.; to soften; to meliorate; to alleviate; to diminish; to lessen; as, to mitigate heat or cold; to mitigate grief. 2. To make mild and accessible; to mollify; -- applied to persons. (old) This opinion ... mitigated kings into companions. Burke. Syn. -- To alleviate; assuage; allay. See Alleviate.
mimicker: 1. One who mimics; a mimic. 2. (Zoöl.) An animal which imitates something else, in form or habits.
misaccompt: To account or reckon wrongly. (old) Chaucer.
miswend: To go wrong; to go astray. (old) "The world is miswent." Gower.
microlite: 1. A rare mineral of resinous luster and high specific gravity. It is a tantalate of calcium, and occurs in octahedral crystals usually very minute. 2. (Min.) A minute inclosed crystal, often observed when minerals or rocks are examined in thin sections under the microscope.
misplacement: The act of misplacing, or the state of being misplaced.
millsixpence: A milled sixpence; -- the sixpence being one of the first English coins milled (1561).
misguide: To guide wrongly; to lead astray; as, to misguide the understanding. | Misguidance; error. (old) Spenser.
mizzy: A bog or quagmire. (old) Ainsworth. M'-NAUGHT M'-Naught" (mak*nalt"), v. t. (Steam Engines) To increase the power of (a single-cylinder beam engine) by adding a small high-pressure cylinder with a piston acting on the beam between the center and the flywheel end, using high-pressure steam and working as a compound engine, -- a plan introduced by M'Naught, a Scottish engineer,…
mirksome: Dark; gloomy; murky. (old) Spenser. -- Mirk"some*ness, n. (old)
millepora: A genus of Hydrocorallia, which includes the millipores.
mithridatic: Of or pertaining to King Mithridates, or to a mithridate.
mineralization: 1. The process of mineralizing, or forming a mineral by combination of a metal with another element; also, the process of converting into a mineral, as a bone or a plant. 2. The act of impregnating with a mineral, as water. 3. (Bot.) The conversion of a cell wall into a material of a stony nature.
milleped: A myriapod with many legs, esp. a chilognath, as the galleyworm. [Written also millipede and milliped.]
mischoose: To choose wrongly. Milton. | To make a wrong choice.
misadventure: Mischance; misfortune; ill lick; unlucky accident; ill adventure. Chaucer. Homicide by misadventure (Law), homicide which occurs when a man, doing a lawful act, without any intention of injury, unfortunately kills another; -- called also excusable homicide. See Homicide. Blackstone. Syn. -- Mischance; mishap; misfortune; disaster; calamity.
millet: The name of several cereal and forage grasses which bear an abundance of small roundish grains. The common millets of Germany and Southern Europe are Panicum miliaceum, and Setaria Italica. Note: Arabian millet is Sorghum Halepense. -- Egyptian or East Indian, millet is Penicillaria spicata. -- Indian millet is Sorghum vulgare.
mislike: To dislike; to disapprove of; to have aversion to; as, to mislike a man. Who may like or mislike what he says. I. Taylor. | Dislike; disapprobation; aversion.
milvus: A genus of raptorial birds, including the European kite.
microspore: One of the exceedingly minute spores found in certain flowerless plants, as Selaginella and Isoetes, which bear two kinds of spores, one very much smaller than the other. Cf. Macrospore.
microscopal: Pertaining to microscopy, or to the use of the microscope. Huxley.
misread: To read amiss; to misunderstand in reading.
micrometrical: Belonging to micrometry; made by the micrometer. -- Mi`cro*met"ric*al*ly, adv.
mink: A carnivorous mammal of the genus Putorius, allied to the weasel. The European mink is Putorius lutreola. The common American mink (P. vison) varies from yellowish brown to black. Its fur is highly valued. Called also minx, nurik, and vison.
misericorde: 1. Compassion; pity; mercy. (old) 2. (Anc. Armor.) Same as Misericordia, 2.
mighty: 1. Possessing might; having great power or authority. Wise in heart, and mighty in strength. Job ix. 4. 2. Accomplished by might; hence, extraordinary; wonderful. "His mighty works." Matt. xi. 20. 3. | A warrior of great force and courage. [R. & Obs.] 1 Chron. xi. 12.
misapprehend: To take in a wrong sense; to misunderstand. Locke.
misword: To word wrongly; as, to misword a message, or a sentence. | A word wrongly spoken; a cross word. (old) Sylvester. Breton.
microvolt: A measure of electro-motive force; the millionth part of one volt.
misincline: To cause to have a wrong inclination or tendency; to affect wrongly.
misprize: To slight or undervalue. O, for those vanished hours, so much misprized! Hillhouse. I do not blame them, madam, nor misprize. Mrs. Browning.
midnight: The middle of the night; twelve o'clock at night. The iron tongue of midnight hath told twelve. Shak. | Being in, or characteristic of, the middle of the night; as, midnight studies; midnight gloom. "Midnight shout and revelry." Milton.
miniment: A trifle; a trinket; a token. (old) Spenser.
miscible: Capable of being mixed; mixable; as, water and alcohol are miscible in all proportions. Burke.
misassay: To assay, or attempt, improperly or unsuccessfully. (old) W. Browne.
mixed: Formed by mixing; united; mingled; blended. See Mix, v. t. & i. Mixed action (Law), a suit combining the properties of a real and a personal action. -- Mixed angle, a mixtilineal angle. -- Mixed fabric, a textile fabric composed of two or more kinds of fiber, as a poplin. -- Mixed marriage, a marriage between persons of different races or religions;
minoress: See Franciscan Nuns, under Franciscan, a.
microphonous: Serving to augment the intensity of weak sounds; microcoustic.
military: 1. Of or pertaining to soldiers, to arms, or to war; belonging to, engaged in, or appropriate to, the affairs of war; as, a military parade; military discipline; military bravery; military conduct; | The whole body of soldiers; soldiery; militia; troops; the army.
microchemical: Of or pertaining to micro-chemistry; as, a micro-chemical test.
micropyle: (a) An opening in the membranes surrounding the ovum, by which nutrition is assisted and the entrance of the spermatozoa permitted. (b) An opening in the outer coat of a seed, through which the fecundating pollen enters the ovule. -- Mi*crop"y*lar, a.
misrepresentative: Tending to convey a wrong impression; misrepresenting.
microtomist: One who is skilled in or practices microtomy.
middleground: That part of a picture between the foreground and the background.
micrococcal: Of or pertaining to micrococci; caused by micrococci. Nature.
microzooespore: A small motile spore furnished with two vibratile cilia, found in certain green algæ.
milk: 1. (Physiol.) A white fluid secreted by the mammary glands of female mammals for the nourishment of their young, consisting of minute globules of fat suspended in a solution of casein, albumin, milk… | 1. To draw or press milk from the breasts or udder of, by the hand or mouth; to withdraw the milk of. "Milking the kine." Gay. I have given suck, and know How tender 't is to love the babe that milks…
mixedly: In a mixed or mingled manner.
millwright: A mechanic whose occupation is to build mills, or to set up their machinery.
